source_caption:
The ending of Big Fish brings the whole movie together by showing that Edward Bloom’s impossible stories were never really about whether every detail was true. They were his way of turning life into legend, and when his son finally tells him one last story, he finally understands that love can be found inside myth, memory, and exaggeration.

Big Fish (2003), directed by Tim Burton, starring Ewan McGregor, Albert Finney, Billy Crudup. A magical and deeply emotional fantasy-drama about fathers, sons, and the stories we tell to make sense of a life larger than reality.

source_details.synopsis: Big Fish is a 2003 American fantasy drama film directed by Tim Burton. It is based on the 1998 novel Big Fish: A Novel of Mythic Proportions by Daniel Wallace. The film stars Ewan McGregor, Albert Finney, Billy Crudup, Jessica Lange, Helena Bonham Carter, Alison Lohman, Robert Guillaume, Marion Cotillard, Steve Buscemi, and Danny DeVito. It tells the story of a frustrated son who tries to distinguish fact from fiction in the life of his father, a teller of tall tales. The film's screenwriter, John August, read a manuscript of the novel six months before it was published and convinced Columbia Pictures to acquire the rights.
